evidence: src/auth/auth.service.ts: `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(randomStringGenerator()).digest('hex')` is duplicated in validateLogin, validateSocialLogin and refreshToken, even though the class already uses a private helper (getTokensData) for token creation.

src/auth/auth.service.ts: `jwtService.signAsync({ confirmEmailUserId ... }, { secret: configService.getOrThrow('auth.confirmEmailSecret'), expiresIn: configService.getOrThrow('auth.confirmEmailExpires') })` appears in both register and update.
src/auth/auth.service.ts: the same verifyAsync try/catch throwing UnprocessableEntityException({ errors: { hash: 'invalidHash' } }) is repeated in confirmEmail, confirmNewEmail and resetPassword.
src/auth/auth.service.ts: the session-create plus getTokensData plus LoginResponseDto assembly is duplicated between validateLogin and validateSocialLogin.

src/auth/auth.service.ts: `bcrypt.compare` is called directly in validateLogin and update, while register/resetPassword pass plaintext passwords to usersService.create/update. Password hashing and checking are split across services.
src/auth/auth.service.ts: the new-user default `role: { id: RoleEnum.user }` is set in both register and validateSocialLogin, each with its own status default.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit is one file, AuthService. It covers one concern: authentication, registration, email confirmation, password reset and session tokens. That part of the rubric passes. It fails the "keep each rule or invariant in one place" part. The class already has one private helper, getTokensData, but several other rules are copied inline instead of being pulled into helpers like it:
1. Session-hash generation is written out three times.
2. Signing the confirm-email JWT (secret plus expiry from config) is repeated in register and update.
3. Verifying a JWT and mapping failure to 'invalidHash' is repeated in confirmEmail, confirmNewEmail and resetPassword.
4. The defaults for a new user (RoleEnum.user, plus a status) are set separately in register and validateSocialLogin.
5. Password checking calls bcrypt.compare directly in two places, while password hashing on create/update is left to UsersService. The password-hashing rule is therefore split across two services.

violations.message: Session-hash generation (sha256 of randomStringGenerator) is duplicated in validateLogin, validateSocialLogin and refreshToken instead of living in one helper. Session creation plus token issuing is also duplicated between validateLogin and validateSocialLogin.

Confirm-email JWT signing (confirmEmailSecret/confirmEmailExpires) is duplicated in register and update. Hash verification with the 'invalidHash' error is duplicated in confirmEmail, confirmNewEmail and resetPassword.

Password checking calls bcrypt.compare directly in validateLogin and update, while hashing is left to UsersService. This splits the password invariant across services and skips the service that owns it. New-user role defaults (RoleEnum.user) are also set separately in register and validateSocialLogin.
